finalization.rule: Finalize only the current incumbent; null means baseline and is allowed only when there is no measured feasible improvement.

instructions: Select one RISC-V custom instruction, or the unchanged baseline. Maximize VERIFIED FEASIBLE whole-program speedup within the measurement-attempt budget. Predictions are uncalibrated, not measurements. Consider all provided heuristics, structure, uncertainty, area, timing and measurement cost. Use only list_candidates, predict, measure and finalize. Every submitted measure request, including an invalid ID or repeat, consumes an attempt; failed measurements also count. No unqueried outcome is available. Only the current incumbent may be finalized: use incumbent.candidate_id exactly, or use null only when incumbent.candidate_id is null. The host computes the best paid, correct, device-fitting, area/timing-feasible improvement; never finalize a stale, unmeasured, infeasible, or lower-speedup candidate. Check remaining.decision_turns_after_this_response and provider_calls_available_including_this_response. Each provider response permits one tool action; reserve a later call to finalize after a measurement. If the remaining decision/provider allowance is exhausted, the host selects its verified incumbent or baseline. You may stop early. The summary you submit is an unverified agent note; the host returns the authoritative measured result. Provide a short decision summary, not private chain of thought. Single instructions only; individual speedups and area cannot be added. This is consumed-data replay, not fresh hardware measurement or an unseen-workload experiment. The request may include current_grouped_ml_bundle metadata. When present, the predict tool returns pairwise_rank_score (an ordering score, not a speedup estimate), pairwise_rank_position, factorized_feasibility_probability and factorized_decision_score for the 64-LUT4 cap. Feasibility scores and their ensemble disagreement are uncalibrated; disagreement is not a confidence interval. The decision score is feasibility score multiplied by the nonnegative public analytic cycle-reduction estimate. Use these current grouped-model outputs alongside merit, frequency and paid evidence; only a paid outcome verifies area, timing and correctness.
